annotations.title: Look up a game key's lowest price

description: The cheapest key for one PC or console game at the 24 shops Keyfinder compares: price, shop, platform, region and edition of the cheapest key in stock that activates in Germany and the EU (PC and the standard edition first, as the game's page shows it), Steam's own price and the saving where known, how many offers and shops were compared, when the prices were read, and the game's page. Where a shop sells an account with the game on it, cheapest_account gives that price apart: it is an account, not a key. With country set to US, CA, AU, NZ, SG, JP, KR, BR, MX, AR, CL, CO, GB it also gives the cheapest key that activates there, in that country's currency too, and the country's page. Use it when someone asks where a game is cheapest, what its key costs or whether it costs less than on Steam. Prices are in euros, read within the last few hours, as the game's page shows them: where a shop's discount code lowers a price, price_eur counts it in and discount_code gives the code to enter at the shop's checkout and the price without it. Some shops add a fee at checkout. If the game isn't the one meant, other_matches lists up to four others. Read-only; Keyfinder records the call (tool, arguments and time).

country.description: Optional two-letter country code for prices there: US, CA, AU, NZ, SG, JP, KR, BR, MX, AR, CL, CO, GB. Other codes get the price for Germany and the EU.

game.description: The game's title, English works best, e.g. Elden Ring.

name: find_game_price

discount_code.description: A shop's discount code that price_eur already counts in, as the Keyfinder page names it. Name the code with the price: the buyer enters it at the shop's checkout.

needs_keyfinder_link.description: true when the code works only in a cart reached through the shop button on the Keyfinder page.

region.description: Where the key activates: EU, WW (worldwide), NA, LATAM, ASIA, MEA, RU or other.

cheapest_account.description: The lowest listed price of an account with the game on it, where a shop sells one. Not a key.
